item.text:
**3B.10 Research Note**
**Verdict:** partial / mixed, leaning **no**. Marcos made some real protection-oriented moves in 2024, especially on flood response, the POGO ban, and the drug-policy shift toward due process. But the best independent reporting still shows persistent drug-related killings, enforced disappearances, red-tagging, and labor intimidation. That is not enough to say citizens were broadly safer than they had been inherited.

| Direction | Claim-level item | Source | Date | URL | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | During Typhoon Carina, Marcos ordered swift assistance and called for a comprehensive national flood-control plan. That is a genuine protection-oriented response to a domestic crisis and could reduce preventable deaths and displacement. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-26 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-calls-for-comprehensive-national-flood-control-plan-to-protect-communities-production-areas/ | 3B.10, 3B.9, 3B.7 |
| Positive | Marcos banned all POGOs after citing torture, kidnapping, trafficking, and murder tied to the industry. That is concrete action against a violent abuse network affecting vulnerable people. | GMA News Online | 2024-07-22 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914272/marcos-announces-ban-on-all-pogo/story/ | 3B.10, 3B.7, 3B.1 |
| Positive | The U.S. State Department report says the Marcos administration refocused the antidrug campaign toward treatment, due process, and rule-of-law investigations. It also notes killings declined versus prior years, though they continued. | U.S. State Department via ecoi.net | 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html | 3B.10, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Positive | The DOJ created a task force to investigate Duterte-era extrajudicial killings and file charges if warranted. That is an accountability move that could reduce future impunity, even if limited. | Philippine News Agency | 2024-11-06 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1237266 | 3B.10, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Negative | HRW’s 2025 report on 2024 says drug-related killings persisted through the year, with more than half attributed to security forces; it also says 14 people were forcibly disappeared under Marcos, with four new cases in 2024, and political violence against local officials increased. | Human Rights Watch | 2025-01-16 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/philippines | 3B.10, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Negative | The State Department report says credible reports of arbitrary killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary arrest/detention, media restrictions, and threats to labor activists remained. That cuts against a clean “citizens are safer” finding. | U.S. State Department via ecoi.net | 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html | 3B.10, 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.8 |
| Negative | HRW says Marcos-era officials and police or military members repeatedly visited and threatened union leaders by linking them to communism, causing fear and withdrawal from unions. This is direct evidence of ongoing intimidation of community organization. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | 3B.10, 3B.8, 3B.7 |
| Negative | Amnesty says Marcos-era actors weaponized digital tools, misinformation, and anti-terror framing to create fear; red-tagging vilified activists, journalists, teachers, and others as extremists or terrorists. | Amnesty International | 2024-10-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/ | 3B.10, 3B.6, 3B.8, 3B.3 |

**Bottom line:** there is credible evidence of partial harm reduction in specific domains, but not enough to conclude Marcos left Filipinos broadly safer from political violence and domestic insecurity in 2024. The strongest counterevidence is the continued pattern of killings, disappearances, red-tagging, and labor intimidation.

**Search gap:** I found little direct 2024 evidence quantifying displacement from intergroup violence specifically. The evidence is much stronger on killings, disappearances, intimidation, and disaster response than on nationwide displacement trends.
